event_summary: A desktop Newton’s-cradle-like object starts with five aligned chrome spheres, then the outer spheres alternately move outward to the left and right while the central spheres stay grouped.
raw_event_description: The video opens on a metal frame with a black base on a wooden table, holding five shiny hanging spheres in a straight row. For an initial interval the spheres appear still. A left-side outer sphere is then seen separated toward the left and moving back toward the row; afterward a right-side outer sphere is seen separated to the right while the remaining spheres stay grouped near the center. The visible motion continues in alternating left and right outward displacements of an outer sphere, with brief moments where the spheres return to a near-straight row. The camera view remains fixed.

reasons: The hanging metal spheres, support frame, strings, base, and tabletop are visible.
The five spheres begin in a straight row with no visible motion.
The camera is already pointed at the setup before the visible motion begins.

The cradle and spheres remain visually still for an initial interval.
The left outer sphere is visible separated to the left of the central row.
The left outer sphere appears blurred during inward motion near the left side of the row.
The right outer sphere is visible separated to the right of the central row.
Four spheres remain grouped near the center while one outer sphere is displaced outward.
At several moments the five spheres appear nearly aligned again in a side-by-side row.
The separated outer sphere alternates between the left side and the right side across the visible sequence.
Near the end, the right outer sphere is again visible away from the central group on the right side.
The support frame, base, tabletop, and blue-and-black item do not visibly change position.
The camera framing remains fixed on the cradle without visible panning or zooming.
